page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is an entry-level virtual machine instance belonging to the g1 family. It features 1 vCPU allocated from a shared physical Intel Xeon processor core running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing 1.7 GB of memory per core, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place the g1-small in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both yield a score of 1076.89, reflecting the constraints of a shared physical core. Memory performance is similarly limited, with uncached read and write bandwidths measured at 10.49 GB/sec and 8.91 GB/sec respectively, while cached read-only small block bandwidth reaches 80.25 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is recorded at 0.54 GB/sec, and Passmark CPU and memory scores are 1263.03 and 792.89, indicating low-tier processing and memory capabilities.

The primary tradeoff of the g1-small is its shared-core CPU allocation, which can lead to variable performance depending on host node utilization. However, this architecture offers high qualitative cost efficiency for resource-constrained, low-utilization tasks. Lacking local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, it is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, microservices, development environments, and simple background tasks that do not require sustained high-performance compute or memory resources.
